terms.gloss: one who prepares the dead for burial

evidence: Sen. Ben. 6.38: dēsignātōrēs et libitīnāriī (Lewis & Short)
terms.gloss: an undertaker, who provides and runs funerals
terms.comment: Post-Augustan (Lewis & Short): Seneca names dēsignātōrēs et libitīnāriī, the masters of ceremonies and the undertakers, together. From Libitina, the goddess of funerals.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 169, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
